questions.question: Sayyid Ahmed Khan founded Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College in _________ in 1875.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aligarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Syed Ahmed Taqvi bin Syed Muhammad Muttaqi **KCSI FRAS, commonly known as **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**, was **an Indian Muslim pragmatist**, **Islamic reformer**, **philosopher**, and **educationist **in **nineteenth-century British India**.
 
• He was **born **on **17 October 1817**, **Delhi **and he **died **on **27 March 1898**, **Aligarh.**
 
• **He was buried beside **Sir **Syed Masjid **on the **campus **of the **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
• **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan **is best known **for the Aligarh Movement **—
 
• **A systemic movement **aimed at **reforming the social**, **political**, and **educational aspects **of the **Muslim community**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• He is also **the founder **of **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
• The **Aligarh Movement **was started by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan **(**1817-98**) for the **social **and **educational advancement **of **Muslims in India**.
 
• It **aimed at social reforms **among **Muslims relating to purdah**, **polygamy**, **widow remarriage**, **women's education**, **slavery**, **divorce**, etc. It wanted to impart a distinct **socio-cultural identity **to **Muslims **on **modern lines**.
 
• He **founded the Scientific Society in 1863 **to **translate major works **in the **sciences **and **modern arts into Urdu**.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, announced the **Partition of Bengal** on **July 19, 1905**, and it was implemented on **October 16, 1905**.
 
• The partition was aimed at dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with a Muslim majority, and **West Bengal**, with a Hindu majority.
 
• The official reason given was to improve administrative efficiency in the large and populous Bengal province, which had a population of over 78 million at the time.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and marked the beginning of the **Swadeshi Movement** (1905-1911), a significant phase in India's struggle for independence.
 
• Due to severe opposition and unrest, the partition was annulled in **1911** by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**

 
 
• Launched in response to the Partition of Bengal, this movement emphasized the use of indigenous goods and boycotting British products.
 
• It saw the rise of nationalist leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• Key cultural aspects, such as nationalistic songs like *"Vande Mataram,"* became symbols of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Challenges:**
 
 
• Bengal was the largest province in British India, making governance difficult, which was cited as the primary reason for partition.
 
• However, critics argued that the real motive was to create religious division and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Reversal of Partition:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British annulled the partition due to the sustained opposition and shifted the capital of British India from **Calcutta to Delhi**.
 
• The annulment is considered a partial victory for Indian nationalists, though it did not eliminate British control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Nationalism:**
 
 
• The partition and subsequent unrest significantly contributed to the growth of the Indian National Congress and the demand for **Swaraj (self-rule)**.
 
• It also led to the unification of Indian leaders across regions and religions to oppose British policies.

questions.question: Who established the Ramakrishna Mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda was born on **12th January**, 1863 in **Calcutta **(now Kolkata). He died in 1902.
 
• His original name was Narendranath Datta. 
 
• He was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, author, religious teacher, thinker, and patriot.
 
• He was the **founder **of the Ramkrishna Mission.
 
• He introduced the Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the world.
 
• In 1893 he gave his famous speech to the World's Parliament of Religions also known as the Chicago speech.
 
• In **1984 **Government decided to celebrate **12th January as National Youth Day.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

 
• **Muni Tarun Sagar** was an Indian **Digambara monk**.

 
 
• Because of their tendency to be frank in their criticism of accepted beliefs and behaviors, his **lectures **are known as **Kadve Pravachan**, or biting talks. His talks have been collected and made available as part of the Kadve Pravachan book series.
 
• In contrast to the bulk of other Digambar Jain monks, he frequently had a predominantly non-Jains audience.
 
• He frequently discussed family and societal concerns in his talks.
 
 
 
• **Gaur Gopal Das** is an Indian monk, lifestyle coach, motivational speaker and former electrical engineer.
 
 
• He is a member of the **International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON).**
 
 
 
• **Jambuvijaya**, also called **Muni Jambuvijayji Maharajsaheb**, was a monk from the **Svetambara sect of Jainism** who belonged to the **Tapa Gaccha order**.
 
 
• His groundbreaking work in the fields of ancient text and Jain Agamas investigation, cataloging, and translation was well known.
 
• He was in charge of unearthing and disseminating several old Jains manuscripts that were hidden away in various abandoned Jain jnana bhandaras (ancient Jain libraries).
 
• He was **Muni Punyavijay's** pupil.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Morely-Minto Reforms were introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Minto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Morely-Minto Reforms__

 __
 
• The **Indian Councils Act 1909** was an act of the** British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.**
 
• It was more commonly called the **Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, the 4th Earl of Minto.**
 
• The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
 
• Indians were given membership in the Imperial Legislative Council for the first time.
 
• **It introduced separate electorates for Muslims. **
 
• The members could discuss the budget and move resolutions.
 
• They could also discuss matters of public interest.
 
• They could also ask supplementary questions.
 
• No discussions on foreign policy or on relations with the princely states were permitted.
 
• **Lord Minto appointed (on much persuasion by Morley) Satyendra P Sinha as the first Indian member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.**
 
• Two Indians were nominated to the Council of the Secretary of State for Indian Affairs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Minto-II (1905-1910):

 
 
• He was the Viceroy of India when the **Muslim League was formed.**
 
• **The Surat Split in the INC took place in the year 1907 AD. **
 
• Swadeshi Movement also took place during his period apart from the formation of the All India Muslim League in 1906.
 
• It was founded in the year 1906 by Aga Khan and Nawab of Dacca, Nawab Salim Ullah in Dacca.
 
• It was formed to promote Muslim interests in British India and enjoyed the patronage, the British.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter is also known as the ‘Grand Old Man of India’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Dadabhai Naoroji__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dadabhai Naroji, the Grand Old Man of India, was a Parsi intellectual, educator, cotton trader, and early Indian political and social leader. 

 
 
• Dadabhai Naroji became the president of the Indian National Congress(INC) three times.
 
• Firstly, He presided over its (INC) second session in Kolkata (then Calcutta) in 1886.
 
• The second time he became the president of the Indian National Congress (INC) at Lahore in 1893 and, later, for the third time again in Kolkata in 1906.
 
• He is widely called "The Grand Old Man of India" for his hard work to attain "Swaraj".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a great social reformer and educationist who provided exemplary leadership to India's freedom movement.

 
 
• He worked towards social empowerment, expansion of education, and struggle for freedom in India for three decades and rejected the use of reactionary or revolutionary ways.
 
• Between 1899 and 1902, he was a member of the Bombay Legislative Council followed by work at the Imperial Legislative Council from 1902 till his death (1915).
 
• At the Imperial legislature, Gokhale played a key role in framing the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909.
 
 
 
• **Zakir Hussain** was the 3rd president of India, from 13 May 1967 until his death in 1969.
 
 
• He is buried along with his wife (who died some years later) on the campus of Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi.
 
• He also served as the Governor of Bihar as well as the Vice-President of India.
 
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was Born in Porbandar on 2 October 1869.
 
 
• ​He died on 30 January 1948.
 
• He was undoubtedly a great man, both in personal force and in political effect.
 
• He was an Indian Lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer who moulded the character of the struggle for freedom in India, and impressed his own ideals upon the new governing class that came into power when the English went home.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.

questions.question: Which among the following is considered the first experiment of Satyagraha by Gandhiji in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha was the first Satyagraha movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in India.
 
• It took place in 1917 in the Champaran district of Bihar.
 
• The movement was aimed at addressing the grievances of indigo farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions by British planters.
 
• Gandhiji employed non-violent civil disobedience and mobilized the local peasants to protest against the exploitative system.
 
• This movement marked the beginning of Gandhiji's active involvement in the Indian independence struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigo Cultivation**:

 
 
• Indigo was a significant cash crop during British rule, primarily used for dyeing textiles.
 
• Farmers were coerced into growing indigo on a portion of their land, often leading to severe financial losses and indebtedness.
 
 
 
• **Non-Violent Resistance**:
 
 
• Gandhiji's strategy of non-violent resistance, also known as Satyagraha, was based on the principles of truth and non-violence.
 
• This approach aimed to bring about social and political change through peaceful means.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Satyagraha**:
 
 
• The success of the Champaran Satyagraha boosted the confidence of Indian farmers and peasants in the effectiveness of non-violent protest.
 
• It also helped in highlighting the plight of the indigo farmers at a national level, garnering support for their cause.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Movements**:
 
 
• Following the Champaran Satyagraha, Gandhiji led several other significant movements like the Kheda Satyagraha, Ahmedabad Mill Strike, and the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• These movements played crucial roles in India's fight for independence from British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following nationalist leaders was popularly known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Chitranjan Das is also known as Deshbandhu.
 
• He was a Freedom fighter and originally belonged to West Bengal.
 
• He was one of the Founding members of the Swaraj Party.
 
• He was associated with Anushilan Samiti.
 
• Anushilan Samiti was active in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dadabhai Naoroji, the “Grand Old Man of India”, was the first Indian member of the British parliament.

 
 
• In 1865 and 1866, Naoroji helped found the London Indian Society and the East India Association respectively.
 
• He was Congress president thrice, in 1886, 1893, and 1906.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was among the key proponents of the ‘Drain Theory’, disseminating it in his 1901 book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’.
 
 
 
• **Ashutosh Mukherjee** was the Educator, Second Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University, and the Judge of Calcutta High Court.
 
• **Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya **was born in Allahabad (now Prayagraj) in Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
• He played a key role in the Indian independence struggle against British rule.
 
• He was given the title of ‘Mahamana’ by Rabindranath Tagore and the second President of India, Dr S. Radhakrishnan gave him the status of a ‘Karmayogi’.
 
• He founded the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916.
 
• He helped establish the Hindu Mahasabha (“Great Society of Hindus”) in 1906.

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was popularly known as 'Master Da'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surya Sen was popularly known as 'Master Da'**__.

 __
 
• **Surya Sen**, also called Surya Kumar Sen (22 March 1894 – 12 January 1934), was an Indian revolutionary who was influential in the Indian independence movement against British rule in India and is best known for leading the 1930 Chittagong armoury raid.
 
• Sen was a school teacher by profession and was popularly known as **Master Da**.
 
• He was influenced by nationalist ideals in 1916 while he was a student of B.A. in Berhampore College (Now Krishnath College).
 
• In 1918, he was selected as **president of the Indian National Congress's Chittagong branch**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashfaqulla Khan** was an Indian independence activist in the Indian independence movement and co-founder of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
 
• **Batukeshwar Dutt **was an Indian socialist revolutionary and independence fighter in the early 1900s.
 
 
• He is best known for having exploded two bombs, along with Bhagat Singh, in the Central Legislative Assembly in New Delhi on 8 April 1929.
 
 
 
• **Ram Prasad Bismil** was an Indian revolutionary who participated in the Mainpuri Conspiracy of 1918, and the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925, and fought against British rule in India.
 
 
• Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil was a freedom fighter who played an active role in India's freedom struggle.
